name: Familial Isolated Clinodactyly of Fingers

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnosis of Familial Isolated Clinodactyly

criteria.description: Radial deviation of the fifth finger(s) evident on physical examination
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No associated syndromic features or other congenital anomalies
Radiographic evidence of abnormal phalangeal angulation without other skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radial deviation of the fifth finger(s) with positive family history and absence of other syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and radiographic findings

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radial deviation of the fifth finger
searchTerms: fifth finger bent toward thumb side

common.symptomName: Mild shortening of the affected finger(s)
Limited range of motion in the affected finger(s)
Familial occurrence with autosomal dominant pattern
Asymmetry in finger length or angulation
searchTerms: fingers of different sizes or angles

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of hand dexterity
Cosmetic concerns related to finger curvature
Tenderness over the affected phalanx after trauma
searchTerms: pain over finger bone after injury

occasional.symptomName: Occasional joint stiffness in affected finger(s)

searchTerms: early signs of wrist nerve issues
joint wear and tear in digit

imaging: Radiographs showing radial angulation of the middle phalanx of the fifth finger without other skeletal abnormalities
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern observed in families
No specific gene mutation consistently identified
other: Physical examination revealing isolated clinodactyly without syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional congenital anomalies or syndromic features
Flexion deformity of the proximal interphalangeal joint rather than radial deviation

redFlags: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Progressive worsening deformity beyond typical isolated clinodactyly
Functional impairment significantly limiting hand use
